title: Shiny
body:
**Shiny** is a framework for building interactive web applications in Python or R without
writing front-end code. The project's dashboard is a Shiny for Python application.

Its model is reactive. The developer declares what depends on what, and the framework
recomputes only the affected outputs when an input changes:

```
user changes the ticker
    -> the data fetch re-runs
    -> every statistic depending on it recomputes
    -> every plot depending on those redraws
```

Nothing in the code says redraw the plot, which is the difference from the imperative approach
in [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]], where an
[[Event Handling|event handler]] explicitly selects nodes and modifies the [[DOM]].
The dependency graph is inferred, and the framework decides what to update, which is
[[PROGRAMMING PARADIGMS|declarative]] in the same sense that [[React]] is.

The application splits into a UI definition describing the layout and a server function holding
the reactive logic, with one module per tab. The calculation modules import nothing from Shiny,
which keeps them testable without starting a server and is [[Coupling and Cohesion]]
applied on purpose.

The trade is the usual one for a framework at this level. Rapid development and a small amount
of code, at the cost of control over the generated interface and a rendering model that has to
be worked with on its own terms.
